statement: Seven people sit around a round table. Each one either always tells the truth or always lies. Each of them says: "At least one of my two neighbours is a liar." How many of the seven tell the truth?

choices.misconception: I took the opposite of "at least one of my neighbours is a liar" to be "both of my neighbours are liars", and with that wrong rule a table of seven liars seemed to work.
I worked out that there are 3 liars and gave that number instead of the number of truth-tellers.
I spaced 2 liars apart around the table and did not check that every truth-teller actually sits next to a liar.
I found that the liars can sit in different seats and thought their number could change too.

hints: What must be true of a liar's two neighbours?
A liar's claim is false, so neither neighbour of a liar is a liar. A truth-teller's claim is true, so every truth-teller sits next to at least one liar. Find how many liars fit both rules.
No two liars sit together, so there are at most 3 liars among seven seats. Each liar together with its two neighbours fills only 3 seats, so 2 liars cannot reach all seven.

solutions.reliable: A liar's claim is false, so both neighbours of a liar tell the truth: no two liars sit side by side, and at a table of seven that allows at most 3 liars. A truth-teller's claim is true, so every truth-teller sits next to a liar. Each liar can sit next to only two people, so with 0, 1 or 2 liars, at most 0, 3 or 6 seats are a liar or beside one, and some truth-teller would have no liar beside them. So there are exactly 3 liars. This really works: liars in seats 1, 3 and 5 each have truth-tellers on both sides, and the truth-tellers in seats 2, 4, 6 and 7 each sit next to a liar. So 7 - 3 = 4 people tell the truth. The transferable idea: turn each type of speaker into a rule about neighbours, then squeeze the count from both sides.

whyOnTest: Truth-tellers and liars puzzles at this level need the false statement negated correctly, "at least one" becomes "none", and then a check on every speaker, liars included.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
